title: ⚔️ Chapter boss ⭐⭐⭐: asking the right question

questions.prompt: Wassim wants to know where his new friend's brother trains. Which question is correct English?

options.text: Where does your brother trains?
Where do your brother train?
Where your brother does train?
Where does your brother train?

questions.explanation: "Your brother" is he, so the helper is "does", and after "does" the main verb keeps its base form: Where does your brother train? The classic mistake is "Where does your brother trains?", which marks the third person twice. "Where do your brother train?" takes the helper kept for I, you, we and they, and "Where your brother does train?" keeps the word order of a statement instead of putting the helper before the subject.

questions.prompt: Hedi wants to know the price of the school trip. Which question is correct English?

options.text: How many does the school trip cost?
How much the school trip costs?
How much does the school trip cost?
How much does the school trip costs?

questions.explanation: A price is an amount, not a number of separate things, so the question uses "how much", and after the helper "does" the verb keeps its base form: How much does the school trip cost? The classic mistake is "How many does the school trip cost?", which brings in the word that counts plural nouns such as buses or tickets. "How much the school trip costs?" has no helper before the subject, and "How much does the school trip costs?" marks the third person twice.

questions.prompt: Read this new member's card: "SCHOOL RADIO CLUB. Name: Khaled Mansouri · Age: 16 · Town: El Kef · Hair: fair · Eyes: grey · Brothers and sisters: two sisters · Reason for joining: to interview local musicians." Which question about Khaled does the card leave unanswered?

options.text: How tall is he?
How old is Khaled?
What colour are his eyes?
How many sisters has he got?

questions.explanation: The card gives his age (16), his eye colour (grey) and the number of his sisters (two sisters), but it says nothing about his height, so the question left unanswered is "How tall is he?" The classic mistake is to expect a height from a card that describes somebody's appearance: "Hair: fair" and "Eyes: grey" give colours, never a measurement, and a height is asked with how + adjective + be.

questions.prompt: Nizar asks Mouna: "Why do you get up at five o'clock?" Which reply gives her aim and not her reason?

options.text: Because I am an early riser.
To revise my lessons.
For revising my lessons.
Because to revise my lessons.

questions.explanation: A purpose is expressed with "to" + the base verb, so the answer that gives an aim is "To revise my lessons." "Because I am an early riser." answers with a cause, which is not what Mouna wants to say. The classic mistake is to translate the link word directly: neither "For revising my lessons." nor "Because to revise my lessons." is used in English when a why-question asks for a purpose.

questions.prompt: Put this question into the past: "Where does your family spend the summer?"

options.text: Where did your family spend the summer?
Where did your family spent the summer?
Where does your family spent the summer?
Where your family did spend the summer?

questions.explanation: In the past the helper "does" becomes "did", and after "did" the main verb goes back to its base form: Where did your family spend the summer? The classic mistake is "Where did your family spent the summer?", which marks the past twice when "did" already carries it. "Where does your family spent the summer?" keeps the present helper, and "Where your family did spend the summer?" leaves the helper after the subject, as in a statement.

questions.prompt: Sami interviewed Emna and now introduces her to the class. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Emna is my new partner. She have got a twin brother and she play tennis.
Emna is my new partner. She have got a twin brother and she plays tennis.
Emna is my new partner. She has got a twin brother and she play tennis.
Emna is my new partner. She has got a twin brother and she plays tennis.

questions.explanation: Introducing somebody moves everything to the third person: "have got" becomes "has got" and the present verb takes -s, which gives "Emna is my new partner. She has got a twin brother and she plays tennis." The classic mistake is to change only one of the two markers: "she play tennis" forgets the -s, and "she have got" keeps the form used for I, you, we and they.
